answer: Each agent can act freely, but to claim a share of pooled rewards it must lock a deposit in a public registry and keep it bonded through a challenge period. Auditors can submit evidence that several identities reuse the same signing key or control pattern; a successful challenge slashes the bond and returns part to the reporter. Creating sybils is therefore not just a matter of minting names: each one ties up capital that could otherwise earn returns. A saffron-market bot may still explore a karst route in an atlas, but multiplying its identities carries a measurable cost.
